verdict.rationale: Postmark documents a complete TypeScript path from install to production, publishes official SDKs for several languages, and provides a test token for trying sends without delivery. A vendor-hosted testimonial claims a five-minute implementation. Copy-paste quickstarts are only evidenced for TypeScript, and the evidence does not show the quickstart surfacing required sender-signature or domain verification up front. Missing for 10: copy-paste quickstarts for non-TypeScript languages, evidence that required sender signature/DKIM setup is shown inline in the quickstart, independent hands-on corroboration of signup-to-first-delivered-email time.

support.subject: As a developer, I can go from signup to my first delivered email in minutes — the quickstart is copy-paste complete for my language and doesn't hide required setup

citations.quote: Install, shared client, template send, batch handling, webhook payload validation, and repair guide — complete TypeScript path from setup to production
Official libraries \- TypeScript \- Python SDK \- Rails gem \- Ruby gem \- .NET \- Java \- PHP
For testing without actually sending emails, use `POSTMARK_API_TEST` as your token.
All API requests require authentication using the `X-Postmark-Server-Token` header with your Server API Token
I just implemented @postmarkapp in like 5 minutes.
